title: How do I install the RamosLabs design tokens in Vue, React, or plain HTML?
summary: Install @ramoslabs/tokens with your package manager, import its CSS once at the app entry, then reference tokens as CSS variables. Or link tokens.css with no install.
short: Install the package with bun, npm, pnpm, or yarn, then import '@ramoslabs/tokens/css' once in your app entry and reference tokens such as var(--color-primary) in your CSS. With no install, add a link to https://design.ramoslabs.com/tokens.css in plain HTML.

sections.heading: Install the package
body: @ramoslabs/tokens is published to npm under the public @ramoslabs scope and is licensed under MIT. Use the install command for your package manager.

sections.heading: Use the tokens in Vue 3 (Vite)
body: Import the CSS once in src/main.ts. The import belongs in the app entry, not in each component. Then reference tokens as CSS variables inside a component style block.

code.label: src/main.ts
code.source:
import { createApp } from 'vue'
import App from './App.vue'
import '@ramoslabs/tokens/css'

createApp(App).mount('#app')

code.label: src/components/SaveButton.vue
code.source:
<template>
  <button class="cta" type="button">Save changes</button>
</template>

<style scoped>
.cta {
  background: var(--color-primary);
  color: var(--color-surface);
  border: none;
  border-radius: var(--radius-lg);
  padding: var(--space-6);
  box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm);
  cursor: pointer;
}

.cta:hover {
  background: var(--color-primary-dark);
}

.cta:focus-visible {
  outline: none;
  box-shadow: var(--shadow-focus);
}
</style>

sections.heading: Use the tokens in React (Vite or similar)
body: Import the same CSS file once in the entry file, src/main.tsx. Then give components a class name and define that class with token variables in a stylesheet.

code.label: src/main.tsx
code.source:
import { StrictMode } from 'react'
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client'
import '@ramoslabs/tokens/css'
import App from './App'

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <App />
  </StrictMode>
)

code.label: src/components/Card.tsx
src/components/Card.css

sections.heading: Use plain HTML without installing anything
body: The token stylesheet is served at https://design.ramoslabs.com/tokens.css. Link it in the head of the page and reference the same CSS variables in your styles. The flat token map is served at https://design.ramoslabs.com/tokens.json.

sections.heading: Use typed values in TypeScript
body: Typed values are exported from the package root. Use them when TypeScript logic needs a token value. For styling, keep referencing the CSS variables, for example var(--color-primary).

code.label: src/brand.ts
code.source:
import { colorIndigo600 } from '@ramoslabs/tokens'

export const brandAccent = colorIndigo600

sections.heading: Components are not shipped yet
body: The DS documents tokens and patterns today. Components with the SJ prefix are planned for the @ramoslabs/vue package in a future release and are not shipped yet. Until then, build UI from the tokens and the documented patterns.

faq.q: Do I need to import the token CSS in every component?
faq.a: No. Import '@ramoslabs/tokens/css' once at the app entry (for example main.ts or main.tsx) or in the root layout. Components then reference the CSS variables directly.
Yes, the tokens are CSS variables, so Tailwind projects can reference them the same way as any other CSS. Import the token CSS once at the root of the app.

faq.q: Can I use the tokens without npm?
faq.a: Yes. Add a link to https://design.ramoslabs.com/tokens.css in your HTML head. The flat token map is also served at https://design.ramoslabs.com/tokens.json.

faq.q: Does the same setup work in React?
faq.a: Yes. Import '@ramoslabs/tokens/css' once in the React entry file, then reference the CSS variables from your component stylesheets.

faq.q: Are the SJ components available to install?
faq.a: Not yet. SJ components are planned for @ramoslabs/vue in a future release. Until then, build from the tokens and the documented patterns.

faq.q: Can I hardcode a color or spacing value while I set up?
faq.a: No. Never hardcode a color, spacing, typography, radius, shadow, or motion value. A raw hex or px value in CSS is a defect, so reference the token variables instead.

howto.name: Install and use RamosLabs design tokens

steps.name: Install the package
steps.text: Run bun add @ramoslabs/tokens, or use npm install, pnpm add, or yarn add with the same package name.

steps.name: Import the CSS once
steps.text: In your app entry (main.ts for Vue or main.tsx for React), add import '@ramoslabs/tokens/css' one time. Do not import it in each component.

steps.name: Use a token
steps.text: Reference tokens as CSS variables such as var(--color-primary), var(--space-6), and var(--radius-lg). Do not hardcode raw hex or px values.

steps.name: Optional: use typed values
steps.text: For TypeScript logic, import typed values from the package root, for example import { colorIndigo600 } from '@ramoslabs/tokens'.

sources: @ramoslabs/tokens package: install commands and exports (/css, /json, root typed values)
DS hard rule: no hardcoded color, spacing, typography, radius, shadow, or motion value
